newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FDA discussed, dropped total cigarette ban.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FDA discussed, dropped total cigarette ban.

text.p: A senior U.S. Food and Drug Administration official said on Thursday that the FDA had discussed a total ban on cigarettes -- but dropped it as not the right public health option.
FDA deputy commissioner for policy William Schultz said that early in the agency's discussions to curb the use of cigarettes "it was clear that a ban was not the right option."
He told the Washington bar association's administrative law and agency practice section that a ban would only drive tobacco underground and do little to end its use.
"When we looked at the health issue," Schultz said, "it was realized that was not the answer."
In the end, he said, the FDA decided to target children because 3,000 of them try cigarettes every day and one-third become addicted and ultimately die of smoking-related diseases.

Asked if the agency's effort to restrict children's access to tobacco were a first step toward further regulation, he said "We view this as a very large program already" and if it works, "fewer adults will smoke."
The FDA's right to regulate tobacco is being challenged by the tobacco industry in a federal court in North Carolina.
